subject: genetics
question: **Type:** calculation A cell picks one of the 64 codons at random, each with equal probability. What is the probability that it is one of the stop codons?
explanation: There are exactly three stop codons, UAA, UAG, and UGA, out of 64 total codons, so the probability is 1/64 + 1/64 + 1/64 = 3/64. A counts only one stop codon, and B counts only two (2/64 = 1/32). C treats the three stop codons as three of the four bases rather than three of the 64 codons.
